concepts.def: Finishing a painting wet-on-wet in one sitting.
Monochrome base layer mapping out values.
Dragging opaque paint over a dry layer.
How warm or cool a colour reads.
Mix of a primary and adjacent secondary.
How light or dark a colour appears in greyscale.

walkthroughs.body_html: Alla prima means "at first attempt". The whole painting is completed wet-on-wet in one session. It demands decisive marks and accurate values — Impressionists like Monet leaned on it to chase changing light.

An underpainting in a single colour (often raw umber) blocks in tonal values before colour is added. Once dry, glazes and opaque colour go over the top. It makes complex paintings far easier to control.

Scumbling drags broken opaque paint across a dry layer for a misty effect. Pair it with attention to colour temperature: warm yellows and reds advance; cool blues and greens recede. Shift both to model 3D form.
